title: subagent: Research Connected Papers bubble sizing

content:
I need to answer a GAIA benchmark question about the DeepFruits fruit detection paper on Connected Papers from 2016.

Question: "On the DeepFruits fruit detection graph on Connected Papers from 2016, what feature caused the largest bubble to be the size it is?"

Please research using websearch and webfetch.

Connected Papers (connectedpapers.com) is a website that creates visual graphs of academic papers. Each paper is shown as a bubble. The key features are:
- Bubble SIZE: represents citation count (number of citations)
- Bubble COLOR: represents publication year
- POSITION: represents similarity based on citation relationships

But I want to verify this is correct. The question specifically asks "what feature caused the largest bubble to be the size it is?" - this might not be just "citation count" in general but could refer to a specific feature or characteristic of the DeepFruits paper itself.

Please try:
1. websearch("DeepFruits fruit detection Connected Papers")
2. websearch("Connected Papers how bubble size works")
3. websearch("DeepFruits Sa 2016 fruit detection citations")
4. webfetch("https://connectedpapers.com/search/DeepFruits")
5. webfetch("https://connectedpapers.com/papers/deepfruits")

Report back what feature causes the largest bubble to be the size it is on the DeepFruits graph.
I'll research this question by searching for information about DeepFruits on Connected Papers and how Connected Papers bubble sizes work.
